title: CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO. Peace of conscience: definition
latin: CAPUT VIGESIMUM SECUNDUM, De pace conscientiae. PAX CONSCIENTIAE est tranquillitas animi in homine credente in Christum, qua fit ut neque perturbetur comminationibus legis, neque frangatur adversis, sed iuxta promissionem divinam liberationem gloriosam ab omnibus quae in hac vita molesta sunt certo expectet tandemque adipiscatur. Oritur a fide reconciliationis cum Deo per D.N.I.C. (Rom. 5:1); fovetur spe quae non confundit; conservatur studio bonae conscientiae.
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO. On peace of conscience.

PEACE OF CONSCIENCE is tranquillity of soul in one who believes in Christ, such that he is neither disturbed by the law's threatenings nor broken by adversities, but according to the divine promise surely expects and at last obtains glorious liberation from all that troubles this life.
It arises from faith in reconciliation with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom. 5:1); it is fostered by hope that does not put to shame; it is kept by zeal for a good conscience.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): It arises from faith in reconciliation with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom. 5:1); it stands as fostered by hope that does not put toward shame; it stands as kept by zeal for a good conscience. — PEACE OF CONSCIENCE stands as tranquillity belonging toward soul in one who believes in Christ, such that he stands as neither disturbed by ye law's threatenings nor broken by adversities, but according toward ye divine promise surely expects and at last obtains glorious liberation from all that troubles this life. — CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO. On peace belonging toward conscience.

title: From justification; sweetness of the heart at peace
latin: Haec est pax quam Angeli Christo nato pastoribus optarunt. Qui vere illuminatus verbo et Spiritu credit Christum passione et morte salutem acquisivisse et per baptismum applicuisse, tranquilla conscientia esse potest. Totum cor dulcedine caelestis pacis conditum est; etiamsi reliquum peccatum in carne sentiat, in Domino laetatur, novit Servatorem peccata in se recepisse et satisfecisse.
english: This is the peace the angels wished the shepherds at Christ's birth. Whoever is truly illumined by word and Spirit and believes Christ acquired salvation by passion and death and applied it in baptism can have a tranquil conscience.
The whole heart is seasoned with heavenly peace's sweetness; even sensing remaining sin in the flesh, he rejoices in the Lord, knowing the Savior took his sins and made satisfaction.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye whole heart stands as seasoned with heavenly peace's sweetness; even sensing remaining sin in ye flesh, he rejoices in ye Lord, knowing ye Savior took his sins and made satisfaction. — This stands as ye peace ye angels wished ye shepherds at Christ's birth. Whoever stands as truly illumined by word and Spirit and believes Christ acquired salvation by passion and death and applied it in baptism can have a tranquil conscience.

title: Against wrath; self-examination; Chrysostom on daily audit
latin: Fumus irae Dei a lege obiectus non reformidatur a pacifico: ubi non est peccatum, non est ira ut merces; castigatio filiorum pacem scientiae non tollit. Chrysostomus monet quotidianum iudicium conscientiae: sedeat mens iudex in animam; scrutare delicta; accusata tua vitia non aliena; ante forum vocata conscientia rationem expetat verborum, operum, cogitationum.
english: The smoke of God's wrath held forth by the law does not terrify the one at peace: where there is no sin, there is no wrath as wages; a father's chastening does not remove the peace of knowledge.

Chrysostom urges a daily tribunal of conscience: let the mind sit as judge over the soul; search out faults; accuse your own vices not others'; before the day, call conscience to account for words, works, and thoughts.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Chrysostom urges a daily tribunal belonging toward conscience: let ye mind sit as judge over ye soul; search out faults; accuse your own vices not others'; before ye day, call conscience toward account for words, works, and thoughts. — Ye smoke belonging toward God's wrath held forth by ye law does not terrify ye one at peace: where there stands as no sin, there stands as no wrath as wages; a father's chastening does not remove ye peace belonging toward knowledge.

title: Absolution and the word; Luther against seeking peace by experience alone
latin: Absolvendus omni studio caveat ne dubitet sibi remissa esse apud Deum peccata. Stare tenetur alterius iudicio non propter praelatum sed propter verbum Christi: Quodcunque solveris super terram. Fides huius verbi faciet pacem conscientiae. Qui pacem alia via quaerit, puta experientia intus, Deum tentare videtur. Tantum habebis pacis quantum credideris verbo. Lutherus resol. de virt. indulg.: etiamsi millies a papa absolvatur, qui verbo non credit nunquam erit quietus.
english: Let the one being absolved take every care not to doubt that his sins are remitted before God. He is bound to stand by another's judgment not because of the prelate but because of Christ's word: Whatever you loose on earth. Faith in that word will make peace of conscience.

Whoever seeks peace another way—say by inward experience—seems to tempt God. You will have as much peace as you believe the word. Luther: even if absolved a thousand times by the pope himself, one who does not believe the word will never be at rest.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Whoever seeks peace another way—say by inward experience—seems toward tempt God. You will have as much peace as you believe ye word. Luther: even if absolved a thousand times by ye pope himself, one who does not believe ye word will never be at rest. — Let ye one being absolved take every care not toward doubt that his sins stand as remitted before God. He stands as bound toward stand by another's judgment not because belonging toward ye prelate but because belonging toward Christ's word: Whatever you loose on earth. Faith in that word will make peace belonging toward conscience.

title: Consummation: eternal life; FINIS Liber IV / Syntagma
latin: X. Consummatio pacis conscientiae et portus verae tranquillitatis, in quem Theologia nostra penetrare cupimus, est VITA AETERNA—finis hominis absolute summus (lib. II cap.14). Proinde nos quoque, cum tanta nos circumdet nubes testium, abiecto omni pondere et peccato, per tolerantiam stadium decurramus, intuentes in fidei ducem et consummatorem IESUM (Heb. 12:1-4; 1 Pet. 1:3-9). FINIS.
english: X. The consummation of peace of conscience and the harbor of true tranquillity, into which our Theology desires to penetrate, is ETERNAL LIFE—the absolutely highest end of man.
Therefore we too, surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, casting aside every weight and sin, must run the race with endurance, looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of faith.
THE END. Liber IV Cap. 22 and the Syntagma densify close at PHYS 1363 FINIS. Index Authorum (PHYS ~1370–1372) is index matter, not densified as treatise body.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): THE END. Liber IV Cap. 22 and ye Syntagma densify close at PHYS 1363 FINIS. Index Authorum (PHYS ~1370–1372) stands as index matter, not densified as treatise body. — Therefore we too, surrounded by so great a cloud belonging toward witnesses, casting aside every weight and sin, must run ye race with endurance, looking toward Jesus ye pioneer and perfecter belonging toward faith. — X. Ye consummation belonging toward peace belonging toward conscience and ye harbor belonging toward true tranquillity, into which our Theology desires toward penetrate, stands as ETERNAL LIFE—the absolutely highest end belonging toward man.
